# swift-fakable

> A Swift macro (`@Fakable`) that generates a `fake()` factory method on structs and enums for building test fixtures. MIT licensed, supports Swift 6.0+.

swift-fakable provides a `@Fakable` macro that you attach to a struct or an enum. It generates a `static func fake(...)` wrapped in `#if DEBUG` (by default — the `condition:` argument selects a custom condition or removes the guard):

- On a **struct**, one parameter per stored property, in declaration order, each defaulted to the value it declares or else by its type (a `public fake()` uses only a literal declared value), forwarded to the memberwise initializer. A property inside `#if` is a parameter only in the configurations that declare it; each clause gets its own `fake()`.
- On an **enum**, a `fake()` returning the case marked `@FakeCase`, else the first case without associated values, or the first case whose values can all be written when every case has them. That case's associated values become the parameters of `fake()`, each defaulted by its type; an unlabeled one is positional (`_ value0:`).
- Tests name only the values they care about: `Item.fake(itemID: "item-1", price: 500)`.

## Default Values

- `String`, `Substring` → `""`, `Character` → `" "`
- `Int`, `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int32`, `Int64`, `Int128`, `UInt`, `UInt8`, `UInt16`, `UInt32`, `UInt64`, `UInt128` → `0`
- `Double`, `Float`, `Float16`, `CGFloat`, `TimeInterval` → `0.0`
- `Bool` → `false`
- `Decimal` → `0`, `Date` → `Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 0)`, `UUID` → the nil UUID, `URL` → `URL(fileURLWithPath: "/")`, `Data` → `Data()`
- `Duration` → `.zero`; `CGPoint`, `CGSize`, `CGRect`, `CGVector` → the zero value, as `CGPoint()` and so on (the no-argument initializer, since `.zero` needs CoreGraphics while Foundation names the type)
- `T?` / `T!` / `Optional<T>` → `nil` (checked before the type name)
- a generic parameter of the enclosing type → no default; the parameter is required
- `[K: V]` / `Dictionary<K, V>` → `[:]`
- `[T]` / `Array<T>` / `ArraySlice<T>` / `ContiguousArray<T>` → `[]`, `Set<T>` → `[]`
- a closure, tuple, `any P`, `P & Q`, or metatype → no default; the parameter is required (a closure is marked `@escaping`)
- any other named type → `.fake()`, so nested models compose when each is `@Fakable`; a type the macro cannot be attached to (another module's type, a class, an actor) joins in by conforming to `FakeProvider`, which is that contract as a protocol: one `static func fake() -> Self`

Matching is on the written spelling, so a type alias for `String` resolves to `.fake()`, not `""`. The spelling is read from the syntax tree rather than from the text, so sugar and longhand agree and a `Swift.` or `Foundation.` qualifier is dropped; a type nested in one of your own, such as `Models.Date`, keeps the `.fake()` fallback. Every default is deterministic, so two fakes of the same model are equal where the model is `Equatable`.

## Key Features

- Structs and enums, with or without associated values
- Access-level-aware generation, `private` through `public`, including `package`
- Optional and implicitly unwrapped optional properties
- Arrays, array slices, contiguous arrays, dictionaries, and sets, in bracket sugar or longhand generic spelling
- Foundation value types: `Date`, `UUID`, `URL`, `Data`, `Decimal`, `TimeInterval`
- Geometry types — `CGPoint`, `CGSize`, `CGRect`, `CGVector` — and `Duration`
- Labeled and unlabeled enum associated values, as the parameters an enum's `fake()` takes
- Nested `@Fakable` models through the `.fake()` fallback, and types you do not own through `FakeProvider`
- Generic structs (generic-typed properties become required parameters) and generic enums
- Per-property defaults with `@FakeValue(value)`, ahead of a declared value and the type's default (the value needs a type of its own: `Role.member`, not `.member`)
- Configurable compilation condition (`@Fakable(condition:)` — `.debug` default, `.custom("FAKING")` / `.custom("DEBUG || UITESTS")`, or `.always`)

## Limitations

- `fake()` mirrors the memberwise initializer: `static` properties, computed properties, and constants that already have a value are skipped, while `willSet` / `didSet` observers stay included
- Struct properties need an explicit type annotation; inferred properties are skipped
- `fake()` calls the memberwise initializer, so an `init` declared in the struct's body is an error unless it takes exactly the stored properties as labels, in order (declare a custom `init` in an extension)
- Only structs and enums; anything else is a compile-time error
- A generic enum is an error only when every case carries an associated value it cannot write (a generic parameter, a closure, a tuple): `fake()` could ask for it, but then it could not be called with no arguments, which is what `.fake()` does; a case with no associated values or with non-generic ones is used instead
- `condition:` is the only argument, and must be written literally as `.debug`, `.always`, or `.custom("CONDITION")`; a condition `#if` would reject is a compile-time error

## Requirements

- Swift 6.0+
- macOS 10.15+ / iOS 13+ / tvOS 13+ / watchOS 6+ / visionOS 1+
- MIT License
